brief.greeting: Good morning. Your ESP32 just got a retro screen, and a Rust chatbot finally went offline.

stories.headline: ESP32 powers retro MDA terminal
stories.body: **Wireless retro display:** Hackaday shows an ESP32 driving an old‑school MDA monitor, turning it into a Wi‑Fi terminal. No extra chips, just code and a few wires.
stories.why: It proves you can revive vintage hardware with a single modern MCU.

stories.headline: Inkling‑2 Mini serves image captions
stories.body: **Compact vision model:** AtomicChat released Inkling‑2‑Mini‑Uncensored in GGUF format for image‑to‑text, already pulling 9,540 downloads on Hugging Face.
stories.why: A tiny GGUF model lets you add OCR‑style capabilities to edge devices without a cloud call.

stories.headline: Jan brings offline ChatGPT to Rust
stories.body: **Rust‑only chatbot:** Jan is an open‑source, fully offline ChatGPT‑like assistant written in Rust, now trending with over 46 k stars.
stories.why: Running a large‑language‑model locally removes latency and privacy concerns for dev tools.

quick_hits.text: **Apple silicon inference:** splash repo offers a C++ engine tuned for M‑series chips.
**64‑M parameter training:** minimind can train a 64M‑parameter model in two hours.
**Speech toolkit:** Sherpa‑ONNX bundles STT, TTS, and speaker diarization for Android and Raspberry Pi.
**Echo Dot upgrade:** DIY PCB replacement lets you repurpose the voice‑assistant hardware.
**Pool automation:** New hackathon project keeps swimming pools clean and safe with sensors.

brief.sign_off: Catch you tomorrow – same code, new tricks.

highlights.title: ESP32 Drives MDA Display For Wireless Terminal
highlights.summary: Hackaday details a project that uses an ESP32 to drive an MDA display, creating a wireless terminal.
highlights.detail: The author repurposes an old MDA monitor with an ESP32, adding Wi‑Fi connectivity for remote command input. The build demonstrates low‑cost retro computing and highlights the ESP32's versatile I/O capabilities. No performance metrics are given.

highlights.title: incoai/splash
highlights.summary: GitHub repo incoai/splash offers a local inference engine optimized for Apple silicon devices.
highlights.detail: The engine runs models directly on M‑series chips, aiming to reduce latency and dependence on cloud services, though specific performance metrics are not provided.

highlights.title: janhq/jan
highlights.summary: GitHub repo janhq/jan provides an open‑source, fully offline ChatGPT‑like chatbot written in Rust.
highlights.detail: Jan runs entirely on the user's machine, eliminating the need for internet access or external APIs, and is positioned as a privacy‑focused alternative.

highlights.title: jingyaogong/minimind
highlights.summary: GitHub repo jingyaogong/minimind enables training a 64‑million‑parameter language model from scratch in about two hours.
highlights.detail: The repository provides scripts and configurations to quickly train a small LLM on modest hardware, targeting rapid prototyping and educational use cases.

highlights.title: k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx
highlights.summary: Sherpa-ONNX is an open-source C++ library that provides speech-to-text, text-to-speech, speaker diarization, speech enhancement, source separation, and VAD using Kaldi‑style models via ONNX Runtime, runnable offline on many devices.
highlights.detail: The library runs on embedded platforms such as RISC‑V and various NPUs (RK, Axera, Ascend) and also on x86_64 servers. It includes a WebSocket server/client and can be integrated into Android, iOS, HarmonyOS, and Raspberry Pi applications without an internet connection.

items.title: Model: AtomicChat/Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-GGUF
items.summary: AtomicChat released Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored in GGUF format for image-to-text tasks, accumulating 9,540 downloads on Hugging Face.
items.detail: The model is optimized for low‑resource environments and supports uncensored content generation. It joins the growing catalog of GGUF‑compatible models, making deployment on edge devices easier. Licensing details are not listed in the brief.

items.title: Model: apple/DepthPro2
items.summary: Apple's DepthPro2 model for depth estimation has received 222 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: DepthPro2 targets high‑resolution depth maps from single images and is part of Apple's push into computer‑vision tooling. The model is available without explicit download metrics, suggesting limited distribution or recent release.

items.title: Model: meituan-longcat/LongCat-Video-Avatar-1.6
items.summary: Meituan‑Longcat's LongCat-Video-Avatar‑1.6 model, aimed at video avatar generation, has been downloaded 3,031 times.
items.detail: The model creates realistic video avatars from input images and is built on a diffusion backbone. Its popularity reflects growing interest in synthetic media creation tools. No licensing information is provided in the snippet.

items.title: A Replacement PCB for the Echo Dot
items.summary: A new PCB replacement for the Amazon Echo Dot is presented as a DIY upgrade for voice assistants.
items.detail: The custom board restores functionality to broken Echo Dots and adds solder‑friendly connectors for easier repairs. It aims to extend device lifespan and reduce e‑waste. Compatibility is limited to specific Echo Dot generations.

items.title: Automation For The Swimming Pool
items.summary: Hackaday reports an automation system designed to maintain swimming pool cleanliness and safety.
items.detail: The system monitors water chemistry, temperature, and filtration cycles, triggering alerts or actions via a microcontroller. It reduces manual labor and helps prevent bacterial growth. Open‑source components are used, but exact hardware specs are not listed.

items.title: Building a Robotic Hand on a Budget
items.summary: Hackaday article discusses challenges in robot control like locomotion and whole-body balance despite recent machine‑learning advances.
items.detail: The piece highlights that while ML has improved manipulation, achieving stable walking and balance in humanoid robots remains an open problem, requiring further research in control algorithms and hardware integration.

items.title: Capturing and Mineralizing Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide
items.summary: Hackaday reports on a method to capture and mineralize atmospheric CO₂ for long‑term storage.
items.detail: The technique involves extracting CO₂ from air and converting it into solid minerals, offering a potential pathway to reduce greenhouse gases, though scalability and energy costs are not detailed.

items.title: Quick WIFI Adapter Through USB
items.summary: Hackaday announces a quick USB‑based Wi‑Fi adapter solution for computers with failed internal Wi‑Fi chips.
items.detail: The adapter plugs into a USB port, providing immediate network connectivity without opening the chassis, and is positioned as a fast fix for hardware failures.
